item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he’s seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things.” RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4 Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. He credits MacIntyre and edge coaches Joe Seumalo and George Frazier with helping him learn the game, particularly pass coverage. Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won’t be able to focus all their offensive line on one side. “Teams have to respect his speed,” Hickle said. “If they don’t, then he’ll run right by them. item.title: Former Bellator champion Patchy Mix cut by RIZIN after disastrous 0-2 run
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - JUNE 07: Patchy Mix of the United States looks on after the bantamweight bout against Mario Bautista of the United States during UFC 316 at the Prudential Center on June 07, 2025 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a difference two years can make. Former Bellator Bantamweight champion and two-fight UFC veteran Patchy Mix has been released by RIZIN after a disastrous two-fight run with the Japanese promotion. According to Dropkick , Mix was removed from RIZIN’s active roster and had the remainder of his contract terminated. RIZIN has not formally announced his departure. Mix was considered one of the best bantamweights on the planet following impressive Bellator victories over Kyoji Horiguchi , Raufeon Stots ( watch highlights ), Magomed Magomedov and Sergio Pettis . His dominant run eventually earned him a UFC contract in May 2025, but his long-awaited arrival inside the Octagon quickly went sideways. “No Love” dropped consecutive decisions to Mario Bautista and Jakub Wiklacz , prompting UFC to release him after just two appearances . Mix then signed with RIZIN and moved up to Featherweight in hopes of rebuilding his career overseas. Unfortunately, things only got worse. The 33-year-old was knocked out by 19-year-old prospect Kyoma Akimoto in his promotional debut at RIZIN 52, suffering the first stoppage loss of his professional career. Mix then moved back down to Bantamweight for a fight against Shoko Sato at RIZIN 54. Mix missed weight by a staggering 6.3 pounds , coming in at 140.7 pounds for the 134.4-pound contest. The massive miss resulted in a two-point deduction, and Mix was unable to win the fight officially under RIZIN’s special rules. Sato ultimately defeated him via unanimous decision . RIZIN CEO Nobuyuki Sakakibara publicly criticized Mix following the weight miss, calling the situation unacceptable. Promotion officials later acknowledged that terminating his contract was a possibility. That possibility has now reportedly become reality. Mix leaves RIZIN with an 0-2 record since joining the promotion full-time and has lost four consecutive fights across UFC and RIZIN. It’s an astonishing fall for a fighter who arrived in UFC with a 20-1 record and a reputation as one of the biggest free-agent signings in recent memory. Mix is now a free agent once again — his third different employment status in less than two years.

item.title: UH's Patrick Overmyer: 'Head was spinning' after taking hard hit in Utah game
item.description: Cougars tight end Patrick Overmyer says he's back to normal now, but said "something wasn't right" after he took a hard hit in UH's loss at Utah. (Charlie Riedel/Associated Press) University of Houston tight end Patrick Overmyer said "something wasn't right" on the play that knocked him out of the game against Utah. Overmyer was hurt on the Cougars' opening drive and did not return in the 21-13 loss to then-No. 10 Utah . Overmyer was upended by defensive back Elijah Davis on a pass that gained no yards. He struck the back of his helmet on the turf and was slow to get up. UH said Overmyer suffered an upper-body injury. "Right away, when I tried to get up, I kind of lost coordination in my legs and my head was spinning and all that type of stuff," Overmyer said after Tuesday's practice. "I knew something wasn't right." Overmyer, who leads the team with seven touchdown catches, sat out the open week and returned to practice Monday as the No. 17 Cougars prepare to host Cincinnati on Saturday. "I'm feeling good, all back to normal," Overmyer said. "(Open) week came at a perfect time. Good week for me to get healthy. I kind of just chilled a little bit. I'm feeling good." item.title: CFP rankings 2026: LSU ranks No. 14 in first playoff rankings
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LA - OCTOBER 03: A detail of an LSU Tigers helmet on the bench during the second half of a game against the McNeese State Cowboys at Tiger Stadium on October 3, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The first College Football Playoff rankings have just been released and while the LSU Tigers are sitting at 6-2, the “experts” have them ranked at No. 14 which puts them just out of reach of making the postseason, if the season were to end today. These initial rankings are a bit skewed as LSU is ranked lower than Tennessee and Alabama, who is ranked above Kentucky despite having a better record. Honestly, the rankings never make sense and it will only get worse once they go to a 24 team playoff system. The week, the Tigers return to action after a much-needed bye week following consecutive victories over Mississippi State and Auburn. Those performances helped LSU regain momentum after a disappointing overtime loss to Kentucky earlier in October. Despite their two losses, the Tigers have shown they can compete with some of the nation’s top programs. Both defeats came on the road against SEC opponents, with LSU falling to Ole Miss and Kentucky by a combined nine points. However, the Tigers will need to continue building their resume if they hope to impress the playoff selection committee and get into the top 12. LSU’s biggest opportunity comes Saturday afternoon when the Alabama Crimson Tide travel to Death Valley for a highly anticipated SEC showdown. Both teams enter the matchup with identical 6-2 records, making Saturday’s contest a potentially defining moment in their playoff pursuits. A victory over Alabama would provide LSU with a significant chance of climbing the rankings. Unfortunately, the road ahead doesn’t get any easier for the Tigers, who will face Texas, Tennessee and Arkansas to close out the regular season. item.title: “Put That in Your Hopper and Smoke It”: Jerry Jones Fires Back at Critics Over Cowboys’ Coaching Spending Amid Disappointing Season
item.description: Jerry Jones © Instagram/@dallascowboys The Dallas Cowboys’ season has shown high promise but yielded no consistent results. The Cowboys, who have yet to win consecutive games, have had many instances of blowing significant leads, a worrying pattern that once again was on display during their 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. While Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer has been put on the hot seat by the NFL world, many have also criticized Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones for his supposed unwillingness to pay top dollar for his coaching staff, especially for Schottenheimer, despite the Cowboys (3-5) being the most valuable NFL franchise at $17 billion, according to Forbes. In a conversation with radio host Shan Shariff and the 105.3 The FAN team on Tuesday, Jerry Jones defended his approach to hiring and compensating coaches. “In the NFL, this is after years of looking at all the teams and all the coaches, there is zero correlation between how much you pay a coach or how many coaches you have as to winning. There is no correlation. And that’s a random sample of years and all 32 teams involved. So, put that in your hopper and smoke it,” Jones said (Timestamp: 0:16). “But the point is, you can be pretty creative in hiring your coaches, you can be creative sometime when you don’t even know you’re hiring the coaches. And so, I’ve had some good experience of hiring people who have never been in the NFL; I’ve had some experience of hiring young coaches, older coaches,” he said (0:47 Timestamp). Schottenheimer is reportedly being paid $4.5 million per season, making him the league’s lowest-paid head coach. The salary is approximately a quarter of what some of the highest-paid NFL coaches make per year. Brian Schottenheimer’s Coaching Journey Before Becoming Cowboys Head Coach The creative hiring process Jerry Jones referenced in his conversation with radio host Shan Shariff on Tuesday primarily referred to the hiring process of head coach Brian Schottenheimer, with his current stint with the Dallas Cowboys being his first as a head coach. Before taking over from Mike McCarthy in the 2025 NFL season, Schottenheimer served as the franchise’s consultant in 2022 and was its offensive coordinator from 2023 to 2024. Before joining the Cowboys, Schottenheimer was the passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach for the Jacksonville Jaguars, a position he held in 2021 for exactly one season. Schottenheimer’s first coaching role in the NFL came as an offensive assistant with the St. Louis Rams under head coach Dick Vermeil. From that point onwards, he has been in a plethora of coaching roles across franchises, with some of the most notable stints coming as offensive coordinator for the New York Jets from 2006 to 2011 and the Seattle Seahawks in 2018, alongside coaching roles with the San Diego Chargers and Indianapolis Colts. item.title: Former Seahawks quarterback Russell Wilson interviews for NC State head coaching job
item.description: The first year of Russell Wilson’s retirement has taken him to the NFL on CBS desk, but year two could see him back on the sideline. The long-time Seattle Seahawks quarterback interviewed for the North Carolina State head coaching job on Tuesday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported. This comes just a few days after it was reported another former NC State quarterback, Philip Rivers, would be pursued for the opening. Sources: former Super Bowl champion QB Russell Wilson interviewed today for the head coaching job at North Carolina State, where he played three seasons. NC State now has two former NFL greats who starred there, Wilson and Philip Rivers, as prominent head-coaching candidates. pic.twitter.com/sMYuHHKA2o — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 4, 2026 Though either one of the former passers would be unconventional hires by the Wolfpack, Rivers at least has some coaching experience, having spent five seasons as the head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama after his first retirement. He’s also soon to have ties to the current roster with his son, Gunner, committed to play for the Wolfpack. Wilson, meanwhile, has spent the entirety of his brief post-playing career as a part of CBS’ Sunday pregame show. But, as an NC State alum and a prominent figure in the football landscape, he could be an attractive head coaching candidate in the NIL era of college football. In three seasons with the Wolfpack, Wilson threw for 8,545 yards and 76 touchdowns across 36 games, and ended his career by leading them to a win over West Virginia in the Champs Sports Bowl. He transferred to Wisconsin in 2011 before being drafted by Seattle in 2012.

item.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No.40 - Larry Micheaux (1984-85)
item.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the third of eight who wore the No. 40, Larry Micheaux. After ending his college career at Houston, he was picked up with the 29th overall selection of the 1983 NBA Draft by the Chicago Bulls. The Houston, Texas native played the first season of his pro career with the (then) Kansas City (now, Sacramento) Kings. He also played for the Milwaukee Bucks before he signed with the Houston Rockets for the final season of his NBA career in 1984. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Micheaux wore only jersey No. 40 and put up 4.2 points and 2.5 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. The most recent collapse against the Arizona Cardinals serves as more evidence that head coach and play-caller Brian Schottenheimer is fundamentally not the guy to help this franchise return to glory. The issues start with Schottenheimer’s bizarre tendencies. He routinely fails to make the basic decisions that would maximize his team’s probability of winning. One example is his weird habit of running quarterback sneaks down at his own goal line. Instead of trusting his playmakers or scheming an effective play, he plays scared and chooses to waste a down, putting the offense in a tough spot. Every time he does this, the Cowboys have punted three plays later. Another example is his treatment of Brandon Aubrey. We all know that Aubrey is one of the league’s most lethal kicking weapons, but Schottenheimer finds ways to turn that into a disadvantage for the Cowboys. Rather than pressing and trying to pick up extra yards to give him a more reasonable field goal attempt, the head coach contentedly runs the ball and settles for a short gain. His confidence in Aubrey treats those situations like an automatic three points instead of working for a shorter attempt. He unnecessarily creates high-stress kicking situations that have resulted in blocks and misses. The team also cannot stop repeating the same mistakes. They look uncoached at times, committing the same self-inflicted errors week after week. Are we sick of neutral zone infractions yet? Every week. Early and often. It’s just the same penalties over and over. It’s become an epidemic. Whatever the coaches are doing to discourage this practice is not working. They keep jumping early. As a play-caller, Schottenheimer is equally frustrating. The team doesn’t have much of a rushing attack, as the offense has struggled to deploy the physical ground game they so confidently promote during the summer. It’s been ineffective, and there have been moments when he has completely abandoned it, essentially acknowledging defeat. That admission might be a little easier to accept if the offense possessed a high-powered aerial attack that many believe should accompany having one of the best wide receiving duos in the league. But they don’t. For some reason, the team’s most explosive receiving weapons are underutilized. Schottenheimer fails to create mismatches, and the offense becomes very stagnant at times. item.title: Dodgers Should Consider Hiromi Itoh as Alternative to Expensive Pitching Targets
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are expected to stay at the top of the market, with Tarik Skubal as their top name, but if they want to add on the fringes , Hiromi Itoh makes sense. Hiromi Itoh’s free agent market Itoh has cut his teeth in Japan with the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters and has 1,000 innings of professional baseball. The Fighters posted Itoh on November 1st, giving him 45 days to sign with an MLB team or return to Japan. With the looming lockout, Itoh will have just a month to find a team, since the league is not extending the window for international free agents to sign. Mar 14, 2026; Miami, FL, United States; Japan pitcher Hiromi Itoh (14) delivers a pitch against Venezuela in the sixth inning during a quarterfinal game of the 2026 World Baseball Classic at loanDepot Park. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Who is Itoh as a pitcher? The Japanese right-hander is 29 and has pitched in the NPB since 2021. Itoh has a career ERA of 2.92 and has been a workhorse on the mound. Itoh’s last season in NPB was solid, with a 3.18 ERA, 34 walks, and 159 strikeouts. He also gave up 16 home runs and 184 hits. The year before, he posted a 2.52 ERA over 196.2 innings. Since breaking through to the pro league, he has pitched at least 150 innings in a season for six straight years. Aug 7, 2021; Yokohama, Japan; Team Japan pitcher Hiromi Itoh (16) celebrates after retiring the USA in the 7th inning in the baseball gold medal match during the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Summer Games at Yokohama Baseball Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Yukihito Taguchi-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters) Itoh isn’t a pitcher on the level of Roki Sasaki or even Yoshinobu Yamamoto in terms of stuff, but he has good command and some finesse. On the Dodgers, Itoh would be a long reliever or a back-end starter, but as fans have learned over the last few years, that role can be elevated quickly if injuries hit. As a rotation piece for a couple of years, Itoh could be worth a look for the Dodgers, especially if they want to continue developing their Japanese pipeline. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Itoh has big-stage experience, playing a role on the 2023 WBC team that won the title, along with Ohtani. The Dodgers have enough depth to survive without a move, but Itoh offers legitimate upside as a versatile middle-rotation starter. Itoh is projected to get a two-year, $18 million deal, according to ESPN , and at that total, a swing to replace one of Kris Bubic or Eric Lauer makes sense.

What everyone wants to know right now is if the defense has turned the corner. item.title: Max Eberl emphasizes Lennart Karl’s importance at Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Bayern Munich faced Atlético Madrid away in the group stage of the UEFA Champions League. In a game where Bayern were, by the accounts of their own fans, the underdogs, Bayern emerged victorious with a comfortable 2-0 win. Goals from Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer placed the Bava rians in eighth position on the table. Karl has long been a controversial subject. The recent decline in his quality and output has been heavily attributed to an attitude problem, making this goal as important for Karl as it was for the team. For the teenager, it meant a chance to show everyone who had deemed him unfit to play for Bayern that they were wrong. Following the game, Max Eberl stepped up to back the youngster, citing his importance. “Lennart Karl is an important player for us. We’ve never questioned that,” Eberl said, as captured by @iMiaSanMia . “He worked just as hard as everyone else today. He was incredibly hard-working, and then he rewarded himself with a goal,” Eberl stated. The refore, Eberl’s statement is perhaps not him simply reiterating that—it could be something else altogether. This may be an attempt to soften the backlash Karl could face for his post-goal celebration: a gesture mimicking babbling and shutting his ears. It is understandable that the vitriol following his recent performances could affect him, but constantly reacting to the audience sends the wrong message. A vicious cycle of criticism and Karl’s subsequent reactions could ensue, and the sad part is that the only person it truly affects is Karl himself. item.title: “My Legacy Can Never Be Erased”: DeWanna Bonner Sends Pointed Message to Trolls Over Ring Chasing Accusations After Another WNBA Finals Heartbreak
item.description: DeWanna Bonner © dewannabonner/IG DeWanna Bonner is taking no prisoners when it comes to “keyboard warriors” trying to tarnish her legacy. The forward has been facing backlash following the Atlanta Dream’s heartbreaking Game 7 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals on Saturday. Much of the criticism has centered on her decision to switch teams midseason for the second consecutive year in what many believe was a ring-chasing attempt to win her third WNBA title before the 39-year-old’s career ends. In a post on her Facebook account, the six-time All-Star sent a defiant message. “So many keyboard warriors on this internet! Narratives being created by people who are just miserable and looking for engagement! I know who I am and what I bring to the table,” she said. Bonner described her short stint in Atlanta as one of the best decisions of her life. She added that the experience and impact went far beyond coming close to winning her elusive third title. She ended her message with another pointed reminder to her critics: “But yall keep trying, it won’t work !! My legacy can never be erased!” Bonner first reached the finals in 2009, when she won her first championship with the Phoenix Mercury. She captured her second title with the Mercury in 2014. However, her three subsequent finals appearances have ended in defeat. She returned to the championship series with the Connecticut Sun in 2022 but lost to the Las Vegas Aces. After parting ways with the Indiana Fever midseason, she returned to Phoenix and made another finals appearance in 2025, only to lose to the Aces again. Her latest run with the Dream also ended in heartbreak, this time against the Valkyries. She struggled throughout the finals, particularly after Game 3. She scored four points on 1-of-5 shooting, including 1-of-4 from 3-point range, in Game 4 before going scoreless in Games 5 and 6, shooting 0-of-2, missing both shots from 3-point range. In Game 7, she scored four points on 2-of-6 shooting and went 0-of-3 from beyond the arc. DeWanna Bonner Drops Cryptic Message as WNBA Veteran Hints at Future After Finals Heartbreak DeWanna Bonner looks like she isn’t ready to call it a career just yet. In fact, the 17-year WNBA veteran finds herself an unrestricted free agent. But while the end of her contract raises questions about her future, Bonner teased that she still has something left in the tank. In a message posted on Instagram, Bonner said: “And as for what’s next? Just remember, if you didn’t hear it from me, you haven’t heard it yet. 😉.” For Bonner, the goal is simple: finish her career on her own terms and, ideally, give it another run next season. As an unrestricted free agent, it remains to be seen whether Atlanta will bring her back or if another team will take a chance on her. At nearly 40, Bonner knows the end will come eventually. item.title: Ex-Steelers QB Russell Wilson Interviews for Head Coach Job
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Russell Wilson during a game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Dec. 25, 2024. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Russell Wilson has interviewed for the head coach vacancy at his alma mater, NC State, according to a report by Adam Schefter of ESPN. Wilson spent three seasons playing for the Wolfpack from 2007-10, before transferring to Wisconsin for his final season of college football. NC State fired former head coach Dave Doeren, who had been with the team since 2013, earlier this season. Despite offers to play as a backup this season, the 37-year-old Wilson formally retired from the NFL in June and has been working as a studio analyst for CBS Sports this season. Wilson spent the 2024 season playing for the Steelers , throwing for 2,482 yards, 16 touchdowns and earning his 10th and final Pro Bowl nod. Wilson spent last season with the New York Giants and started three games before an injury forced him to give way to Jaxson Dart. Wilson spent most of his career with the Seattle Seahawks after they selected him in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft. With Seattle, Wilson won NFL Rookie of the Year, led the NFL in touchdowns and passer rating and was named the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year, in addition to winning Super Bowl XLVIII at the end of the 2013 season. Wilson was traded to the Denver Broncos in 2022. Two years later, he was released and joined the Steelers for a one-year run as the team’s starter Wilson is not the only former NC State and NFL quarterback involved in the derby to repalce Doeren, as former Wolfpack and Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Philip Rivers is considered the front-runner. item.title: Bruno Fernandes insists Man Utd 'don't need to save anyone's job'
item.description: Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes warms up prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Bruno Fernandes insists Man Utd 'don't need to save anyone's job'») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes said the players "don't need to save anyone's job" after they fought back from 2-0 down against Roma to win 3-2 and halt a nine-game winless run. United's struggles on and off the pitch this season have seen them slide to 17th in the Premier League, above the relegation zone on goal difference, while they had lost two of their first three Champions League games. Manager Michael Carrick has come under increasing pressure and his future looked bleak as they trailed 2-0 to Roma at half-time at Old Trafford, before Fernandes converted a twice-taken penalty and Matheus Cunha's double snatched victory before the Brazilian's stoppage-time dismissal. Asked if this win had saved the manager's job, Fernandes told Prime Video: "No, we don't need to save anyone's job. "The club needed that win, the players needed that win. We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together. "It's been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media. A lot of lies around many things that have happened between me and the manager, that we have cleared the air, then after that the manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I'm not performing. "Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. "It doesn't change the belief I have of the manager and the staff and every player in this club. It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me." United next face Aston Villa at home in the Premier League on Sunday and Fernandes is hoping their comeback win over Roma can kickstart their season and lift their fans. "They've been used to seeing this club at the top, winning trophies, winning games every week and for them it's been so frustrating to see the club in this situation," he added. item.description: The debut College Football Playoff rankings show the power of being unbeaten. Miami does not have the wins to match one-loss teams such as Georgia, Indiana and Kentucky, not to mention two-loss contenders such as Texas, Alabama and Tennessee. But being one of only three unbeaten teams in the Bowl Subdivision helped land the Hurricanes at No. 1 in the first rankings of the 2026 season , ahead of the No. 2 Georgia, No. 3 Utah and the No. 4 Indiana. Miami has a very good win against No. 16 Wake Forest and two lopsided wins against a pair of opponents with a winning record in Clemson and Pittsburgh. Only two of eight wins have come by a single-digit margin. The Hurricanes should feel confident in their ability to hold onto the top spot by running the table in the regular season. That quest begins on Saturday with a huge matchup against Notre Dame, ranked No. 11 by the committee, in what could be a playoff eliminator for the Fighting Irish . Miami, the SEC and Ohio State lead the winners and losers from the first playoff rankings: Winners The SEC While Miami took the top spot, the SEC owned the debut rankings with four teams in the top seven and nine teams overall in the Top 25. After Georgia, the list of ranked SEC teams features No. 5 Alabama, No. 6 Kentucky, No. 7 Texas, No. 10 Mississippi, No. 13 Tennessee, No. 14 LSU, No. 18 Missouri and No. 21 South Carolina. That the conference has just two one-loss teams heading into November is a little concerning given that no three-loss team has earned an at-large playoff berth without winning or playing for the conference championship. But having this many teams in the first rankings speaks to how the committee currently views the SEC as the strongest of the Power Four leagues, and rightfully so. Come early December, this perception should overcome playoff history to land at least one and potentially multiple three-loss teams in the bracket. Before Tuesday night, the thought was that Alabama had to win this weekend against LSU to stay alive in the playoff race. item.title: New York Liberty fire head coach Chris DeMarco after just one season
item.description: Chris DeMarco has been fired as head coach of the New York Liberty. (Ellen Schmidt / Associated Press) The New York Liberty have fired Chris DeMarco after just one season as head coach, the team announced Tuesday. DeMarco, who had no prior WNBA experience, led the Liberty through a rocky season that included a Commissioner’s Cup win in June before eventually finishing 26-18 and earning the No. 8 seed for the playoffs. The team swept the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx 2-0 in the first round, becoming the fist No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in league history. But the Liberty were then swept 3-0 by the Atlanta Dream in the semifinals. The series included a massive Game 2 mistake by the Liberty coaching staff of not knowing they had a reset timeout left to use in the final seconds of the 101-98 loss. Read more: Valkyries defeat Dream in Game 7 thriller to capture WNBA title in their second season After the Liberty were eliminated, DeMarco said he expected to return for the 2027 season. Instead, the franchise will be looking for its third head coach in three years. This will also be Liberty General Manager Jonathan Kolb‘s fourth coaching search since 2019. DeMarco was named head coach of the Liberty in December, after the franchise chose not to renew former head coach Sandy Brondello‘s contract for the 2026 season. A former WNBA player as well as longtime head coach of the Phoenix Mercury, Brondello’s four-year tenure with New York included leading the team to its first ever WNBA championship in 2024. A former assistant coach with the Golden State Warriors, DeMarco arrived to New York with 14 years of NBA experience as well as having served as the head coach of the Bahamas Men’s National Team from 2019 to 2025. When asked during his introductory press conference in December about how he was preparing to coach women for the first time in his career, DeMarco said he had “ordered every book on the New York Liberty you can find online.” Following their final loss to Atlanta, Liberty stars Breanna Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones did not have much to say regarding DeMarco’s future with the franchise other than it wasn’t their decision. You’d have to go even further back to 2002 to see the last time they hoisted a conference championship trophy. For the better part of a decade, the Leathernecks have not been much to write home about nor have they been more than a blip to most college football fans. Their move to the Ohio Valley Conference a few years ago flew largely under the radar because were and have not been a good team. Now three seasons into their new digs and no longer getting bullied around by the Missouri Valley, though, that all may finally be changing. For the first time in a long time Western Illinois has life, sitting at 5-4 and tied atop the OVC standings heading into the final month of the regular season. And, while lots of variables can be attributed to their newfound success, there is no denying that their electric fifth-year quarterback is perhaps the biggest reason why. Kennedy McGill is a game change in every sense of the word. That’s something that was not hard to see over his last three seasons at Central Washington. McGill was one Division II’s best quarterbacks with the Wildcats. Last year he was named the Lone Star Conference’s Offensive Player of the Year as he led CWU to a league championship. He passed for 1,637 yards and ran for 1,040 while accounting for 34 touchdowns with them coming on a perfect 17-17 split. All of that was probably why Western Illinois head coach Joe Davis gave him a call last offseason. The Leathernecks brought McGill in to compete for the starting job with sophomore Carson Carswell. While Carswell saw some action early on, it was McGill that ultimately won the battle and, after the last few weeks he’s had leading the offense, it’s hard to imagine anyone being a better fit. McGill has put up some truly ridiculous numbers since the start of October and, particularly his ability to run the ball, has been on full display.
